source.publication: 2025 Montana Individual Income Tax Return Form 2 and Form 2 Instructions
source.section: Form 2 PDF p1 lines 1-8 and PDF p2 worksheet lines 1-13; Instructions PDF p12-13 lines 1-8; PDF p17 tax calculation; PDF p18 rate tables; Instructions PDF p13 Line 6, $5,660 subtraction for taxpayers 65 and older; Form 2 PDF p1 line 6; record base.deductions age_65_subtraction

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 1) 80,000.00 = 80,000.00. Federal taxable income = 80,000.00 - standard deduction 33,100.00 (31,500.00 + 1 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older) = 46,900.00 (federal senior deduction ignored, although Montana's line 2 would take it). Filing status married filing jointly, no Montana standard deduction or exemptions. Schedule I Part I: line 7 additions 0.00; line 24 subtractions 0.00. Form 2 page 1: line 1 federal AGI 80,000.00; line 2 Form 1040 lines 12e and 13b 33,100.00; line 3 46,900.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 0.00; line 6 age 65 subtraction 1 x 5,660.00 = 5,660.00; line 7 Montana taxable income 46,900.00 + 0.00 - 0.00 - 5,660.00 = 41,240.00. Page 2 worksheet: line 1 taxable income 41,240.00; no net long-term capital gain, so lines 2-10 are skipped and line 11 is 0.00; line 12 ordinary income tax from the PDF p18 rate table: 4.7% x 41,240.00 = 1,938.28; line 13 = 1,938.28, carried to page 1 line 8. Bracket schedule as numbers (the expected figure): 4.7% x 41,240.00 = 1,938.28. Line 9 nonrefundable credits 0.00; line 10 tax after credits 1,938.28. The 65-or-older spouse (person 0) has no income; the subtraction has no income kind, so it still comes off the return's federal taxable income.
